content.text:
The code already draws the connector lines between the new-context toggles, and it holds up when rows have different heights, so I didn't change any app code. I only strengthened the test. I haven't looked at it in the running app.

**How it works:** each queued prompt's switch sits in a narrow column that spans the row's full height, including its padding. The line runs from the top of that column to the top of the switch, and from the bottom of the switch to the bottom of the column. Since rows sit directly against each other, these pieces join into one continuous line from one switch to the next. That's in `render_queue` in `src/prompt_mode.rs`.

**The test:** I made the middle prompt long enough to wrap, so its row is taller than the others, and added two checks to `queued_context_lines_run_between_the_switches`:
- every switch is centred in its row, including the taller one;
- the rows really do differ in height.

The existing checks also still pass with the uneven rows:
- the line runs unbroken from the bottom of one switch to the top of the next;
- nothing is drawn under a switch;
- a prompt that starts a new conversation isn't joined to the one above.

All 9 queue tests pass. The full suite has only the 4 failures that were already there before this work: the three prompt-wording tests and `code_tasks_sent_to_spec_are_told_what_the_code_task_did`.

If the lines still look wrong in the app, tell me what you see: gaps in the line, the line off-centre from the switches, or the wrong prompts being joined. The layout under test matches the spec, so the issue is likely something the test doesn't cover, such as a particular window size or display scale.
